la:noun:gyrus.html:
gȳrus, i, m., = γῦρος,
a circle, esp. that which is described by a horse in its movements (mostly poet.; cf.: circus, circulus, orbis, orbita).
Lit.: nec equi variare gyros in morem nostrum docentur,; so of a circular course, ring, for horses, : carpere gyrum,: curvo brevius compellere gyro,; ; ; et saep.: adytis cum lubricus anguis ab imis Septem ingens gyros, septena volumina traxit,: ducensque per aëra gyros Miluus,: apes gyros volatu edunt,: grues gyros quosdam indecoro cursu peragunt,: quem (turbinem) pueri magno in gyro...intenti ludo exercent,: in gyrum Euripo addito (in Circo),i. e. around, round about,.—
Transf., the place where horses are trained, a course (poet.): gyrum pulsat equis, (4, 13), 11.—
Trop., a circle, circuit, career, course: mensis artiore (quam annus) praecingitur circulo; angustissimum habet dies gyrum,; cf.: seu bruma nivalem Interiore diem gyro trahit,: similique gyro venient aliorum vices,circuit, course,: homines secundis rebus effrenatos tamquam in gyrum rationis et doctrinae duci oportere,: oratorem in exiguum gyrum compellere,; (4, 2), 21; cf.: attrahe vela Fortius et gyro curre, poëta, tuo,: in dialecticae gyris consenescere,.

la:verb:gyro.gloss: to turn in a circle, wheel around, rotate
senses: to turn in a circle, wheel around, rotate
la:verb:gyro.html:
gȳro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
gyrus
.
Act., to turn round in a circle, wheel round (post-Aug. and very rare).—
Lit.: animal difficile se gyrabit,. —
To go around a thing: omnes greges,; id. Judith, 13, 12.—
Neutr., to turn around: post tergum eorum,: per viam,: per meridiem,: ; Serm. 12, § 20.—
Transf.: gȳrātus, made in a circular form, rounded: chlamys orbe gyrato laciniosa,.
la:verb:gyro.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:noun:gymnasium.html:
gymnăsĭum, ii, n., =γυμνάσιον,
a public school among the Greeks for gymnastic exercises, a gymnasium.
Lit., ; ; ; ; ; : virgineum (in Sparta),; ; ; ; ; —Comically: gymnasium flagri, qs. school for the scourge, whipping-post, a term of reproach applied to one who is often flogged, ; cf.: totus doleo, ita me iste habuit senex gymnasium,i. e. he has belabored me so,.—
Transf., a public school among the Greeks, a highschool, college: omnia gymnasia atque omnes philosophorum scholae,; ; ; : quae vix in gymnasiis et in otio Stoici probant, prooem. 1.— Transf., of a college-building on Cicero's Tusculan estate: cum ambulandi causa in Lyceum venissemus (id enim superiori gymnasio nomen est), etc.,; cf. .
